Name: Sara Stone
Question: Are Ouija boards really dangerous in a way that a demonic entity can be let in?
Answer: Yes. The imagination is one of the most important, potent, creative faculties at mankind’s disposal. The use of speculation, when it comes to matters involving the future, whether it is in “sports” like gambling on the horses or the slot machine, or using a “magic” board to let you in on secrets makes the human mind search for the unknown and to some extent unknowable (except through God) IN the unknown… It’s like going to a ballot box and voting on Door Number 1 without knowing what is behind door number 1. This kind of non-thinking, yet pining for some sort of “significant” or meaningful result raises the fear or anxiety level in a person, which also makes one prone to grasp any straw that volunteers itself. If the good can come through this way (and it doesn’t, for the good is not imprecise nor wishy washy nor speculative per se), then so can the bad. Therefore, stay away from these things. It is your desire to have something for free (as opposed to seeking counsel from God with whom you are in a relationship) that allows the dark side to bind you. You are volunteering for the bondage. Why go slave when you can be a free man?

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is the one thing you feel you need to have to be truly content with your life, and what all would you sacrifice to get it?
Answer: Number one thing: Reparations to all I have done wrong to or harmed, financially or otherwise. Especially, to my son, now an adult, whom I wronged through mistreatment. What all would I sacrifice to get it? First, my limited mindset about how best to produce financially has to go. Heretofore, I have operated out of only one framework: Start at the bottom, work hard, and rely on others to advance you. I need a better strategy. Presently, my son (and roommate) brings in more income than I; he is putting more money out for our overhead. It is reasonable, therefore, to be experiencing pressure to do better, both from within, and from without. Old habits die hard. They must be replaced by new ones with more payoffs. The biggest temptation is to hurry up and end the pain of cognitive dissonance, to get back up on that horse again, to once again join the majority of America’s lower-wage earners in a job with no benefits, where you don’t even know your schedule or number of hours from week to week, let alone are enabled to participate in a health insurance network that is worth your heard earned dough. But at least I’d be “doing my best,” right? “Doing right,” by “carrying my fair share,” isn’t that right? WRONG. All I would be doing is all that I have ever done before and it has NEVER worked. It ISN’T realistic that such an approach would ever work; it is an approach that has only functioned to bind me, to keep me down. You sit there in those positions, doing your best, all the while stilling your anger and discontent and reality-based worry about your future, thinking, “I’m doing the right thing;” Consoling yourself, “What else can be done?” Repeating mantras like, “It isn’t all my fault, that’s just the way things are.” Or worst of all, “Don’t worry, it’ll all be over soon.” I cannot and will not do that crap ever again in my life, period. So…. NEW STORY!! I’m flying off, like a straight-edged tangent, bouncing off that circle of enclosure over options that will never open to a different reality, earnestly applying myself instead to simple things, in order to change what has been the status quo in my life for years. I am shutting down what has been my modus operandi and risking being exposed for a phony, an ignoramus, an under-achiever who’s actually just stupid, or dumb, or whatever I think I might “really” be. Simple things first: I am treating my son with more kindness; finding ways to negotiate and stand up for myself with less scream and more “you and me,” not just me; focusing on progress and insisting I make some; making sure there’s something in it for him. In so doing, I am protecting that part of me that conceives; the heart/spirit/brain-womb in me, that captures reality potential floating through the air, that cannot lite upon the dry hard pan ground of sheer drudgery. Instead, I am refusing to off that fertile body’s offspring before it gets a chance to grow. I am protecting it, and in so doing, I am protecting me. Interestingly enough, it seems that baby ideas, like little babies in the human womb, only survive in safety, with something to hang onto. It’s not enough that an idea is good. Or, perhaps in respect of one of America’s biggest over achievers, Jeff Bezos, I can agree that inspiration is 1%, 99% of success is in execution. The support of branches, of a sturdy vine, a labyrinth of options to shelter that baby from what would strike it down, is what comes next. Therefore, besides setting aside many personal patterns related to having a work life that’s DOA, another sacrifice I must make is to let go of control in the establishing of and maintenance of relational connection with others. For the ideas I wish to incubate are nearly all related on one level or another to community building; I like seeing other people pick up the power cords to their own abilities and plug them in. Most of my ideas are related to improving the chances of that happening for individuals by establishing frameworks for community interaction that highlight both needs and opportunities - where the exposures of both of these sides of the coin of life exponentially increases the number of ways in which individuals can exert their own opinions and utilize their usually under-utilized skills, talents and abilities for the common good. I believe we human beings were made to function together like this. So, I am letting myself out of the prison yard of compulsion and death, and moving into the wilds of personal interactions with mindfulness of mutual respect and keeping an open mind, because you never know what you have that someone else needs, or what they have that you might need, or, in the case at hand, that your idea might need. My desire is to meet my goal of furnishing my son and others with full reparations by using my abilities to perceive and conceive, to let people see how amazing God is and what good ideas He has by setting aside all my junk and let HIM birth good stuff out of me. Thank you for asking to answer this, Mr. Deer. I hope it is helpful to some one out there.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How does Benny Hinn get people to fall down and act like they do once they are on the ground?
Answer: I thought it was phony. I had a then-older friend who had a mess of a house, a terrible childhood, widowhood from a man whom she might have been surely better off without as he used to beat her and their son, and she LOVED Benny Hinn. She was also a VERY powerful “prayer” warrior. Phenomenal at prophecy, though extremely humble and nearly non-existent ego. When I would stop by or call and hear Benny Hinn in the background, I said nothing, but I would just think, perhaps as you or MANY others do, “Well, if that comforts her, more power to her!” WOW, was I arrogant. I had NO idea this stuff was real. I mean NONE. Makes sense though, doesn’t it? For some of us who jump to conclusions that because our experience hasn’t been a certain way, a certain experience must be manufactured, false, or made up? I think so. Well, after my friend died, my son and I were invited to visit a Friday night meeting with a lady “prophet” who “walked in healing” and so on, (those quotes mean she has the spiritual gift(s) of healing and prophecy). People were going up and “getting slain by the spirit.” I thought, okay, what the heck… when my son asked if he should go up. I said sure, if you want. My son has some very special gifts anyway, and I had learned to trust his judgment on certain things, but I sure as heck didn’t need it. He went up, the lady put her hand on his chest, without any force really, then looked up at him when he didn’t “go down.” She stepped back and thought, or prayed, or both, and then put her hand on him again, with a little more force, and WHOMP, he went down and stayed down. Now, skeptics may feel, or conclude, this is hocus pocus, she pushed him down. Nah, my kid was 6′2″ and 170 pounds then and I can guarantee he wasn’t “pushed” down… But, you say, auto-suggestion… Nah, my son IS gullible in some ways… but NOT in this manner. He takes spiritual stuff seriously. He knows it’s not a game and he doesn’t take anyone else’s word, including his mother’s, for anything. Stubborn “young” fool that he is. Anyway, truly, he sorts it all out himself. Well, he went down and stayed down for a bit; when he came back to the chair next to me, he just felt to me to be a bit more relaxed. Okay, REALLY relaxed. But he didn’t say much to me about it until much much later, a couple YEARS later. We went to visit Charis Bible College here in Colorado Springs, Colorado, one Sunday for a special healing service where they had arranged to bring in a world renown “healer.” He had called on the Wednesday prior to let them know he couldn’t make it…. he was worn out and needed rest, and so he cancelled What were Pastor Lawson Purdue and Andrew Wommack to do? Well, they decided to go ahead and have the event, and they put themselves wholly into the event. My son and I were sitting in the back. There was a long time period after a lesson of sorts, of people of all ages sizes and shapes ministering to those who asked for healing all around the large auditorium off of Elkton (this is before their move up to Woodland Park). A minister of Lawson’s came up to me when I was interceding while others were praying for a woman wheelchair-bound with multiple sclerosis. “Ma’am, Do you need healing?” “Oh, no, I’m fine, I’M PRAYING FOR OTHERS,” I proudly announced, because you see, NO ONE’S GONNA fool around with MY BODY, MY HEALING, MY SPIRITUAL LIFE…. I’m no fool!!!! Oh, but what a fool I was, my intellect pierced through with pride. Fortunately for me, the band of do-gooders around this one woman in the wheelchair dissolved, and all of a sudden, I find myself faced with this Texan in a 10-gallon hat, saying, loudly, “MA’AM, may I pray for your?” And barely before I could get a syllable out, this guy has his hand on my neck, and I start feeling this INCREDIBLE feeling, this warmth, like I have never felt before in my life, or since. AND THEN this thing started happening… It was like a humongous, hot flapping butterfly was on top of my head, flapping his wings up and down, up and down, but I wasn’t letting go. I looked around, I weigh a good deal, and I thought, I am not going down with catchers around me… there seemed to be none; the phenomenon continued, all of a sudden, my son was behind me with another man, THEN I remembered what my son had finally told me one day about his experience with that lady, “I just knew, Mom, that if I let go it would feel really, really, good.” I let go. BAM… I went down into those men’s arms and laid on that floor for a bit. I had never had anything like this happen to me, though I was filled with the Holy Ghost when I had a priest in the Episcopal Church lay his apostolic bishopy hand on my head for confirmation in sixth grade… (I began to speak in tongues afterwards but did not know what that was). But, the most amazing thing about this experience, is that it didn’t end. For TWO WEEKS solid, I was in another world. It was like, and believe, me, I had never ever ever put these silly sounding words together in the same sentence before, and no, no one told me this is what you say, or what not, but it was like a few drops of “golden anointing oil,” had been spread throughout my whole being. It was one of the loveliest experiences I have ever had in my life. So, that’s MY experience. But it wasn’t about Benny Hinn. This one is: Todd White was meeting a drug dealer. Addicted to porn by age 10, drugs by 12, this then teen-ager, had conceived the brilliant plan (a way to get yourself shot, actually) to cheat a drug dealer by pretending he was an undercover cop and demanding on the goods…. When the shots started to ring out from the dealer’s 9mm, White was standing next to his car and only about 10 to 12 feet I think it was from the gun. The bullets did not hit him; It was as though they went THROUGH HIM into other objects around him. He got in his car and sped off in total shock and freaked out then heard a voice, “I took those bullets for you, Todd.” Great, Todd thought, now I’m f***ed with the dealer, gonna get killed, AND I’m losing my mind. But there is was again. And then he told Todd he was Jesus. Which freaked him out ever more. So, without going into more detail, Todd was saved that night, and began growing in the Lord right away, but was not getting the results he wanted. He wanted his laying of hands on people to work, just the way the bible says. He wanted to see the blind see and the deaf hear and lame walk. So, he decided to try some Christian conferences. At one, he decided to sit up front. All of a sudden, the speaker pointed at him and told him to come up front. Todd was surprised, but went up. The man looked at Todd, who was several feet from him, with two very large men behind him to “catch” him or help if anything went down. All of a sudden, the man said something, made a move with his arm toward Todd, and TODD AND THE TWO CATCHERS went up in the air four feet and BACK six feet as they heard what sounded like crackling in the air… something like thunder. Todd was stunned, the catchers were caught off guard. And as Todd came around, and sat up and then stood up, he stood in front of the man once more, and said, “AGAIN.” BOOM, up four feet (with the other two BIG guys, again) and back six. Todd was discombobulated. Could not speak. Was receiving power from on high and did not know his name hardly. The two ushers gathered their wits, readied themselves to carry Todd off the stage, then the man of God said to the Man of God, “I NEED MORE OF JESUS;” and ONE MORE TIME. Todd, he says in more than one testimony, was reduced to tears. They literally had to carry him OFF stage, and set him on the floor, where he remained in tears, sobs and so forth for the rest of the event. Now, that man, Todd, he’s got some courage. And the man standing in for God to wipe him out and see that he would be imbued with God’s power? Benny Hinn.

Question: Since I moved back to my parents about 4 months ago, my father keeps getting really angry and talk pretty ugly to me, and most of the times he's around I feel like he really doesn't want me to be here. What's wrong with us…?
Answer: Sorry to hear you are facing this kind of stress in the midst of an already weird and uncomfortable time. When my child was very young, say between four and six, we visited a store on the westside - a discount, re-sell place. They have the old circular clothing racks there, perfect for a child to hide under….! All of a sudden, though I kept really good watch over my son, he was gone! Inside, of course, I panicked! Then I saw some clothing moving under a rack a good 15 feet away from me, and was so relieved to find him under there. I remember doing the same thing myself when my mom would drag me along to stores. BORING! And that’s what I thought this kind of behavior is about… just being bored and looking to play. Years later, however, my son told me one reason why kids might do that behavior. The young of other mammals, and our little children as well, “know” when mom, their chief protector most of the time, is TIRED. Running off to a safe, sheltered, dark place and hiding can be a defense mechanism that is based in instincts! What an insight! Makes total sense to me now! What does this have to do with your Dad? I’m thinking, instinctively, he is pushing you away and being hostile due to CO-VID 19 and its very real threats against your life and his. It is entirely unnatural to keep social distances up, especially with people we know… Doing so causes tension, and keeping on our toes about this practice makes many people (might I say ALL?) uptight. I think you might want to consider that your dad is worried, and at moments he might not even admit to himself, he is worried about somehow hurting YOU by being sick himself and not knowing it. Words won’t comfort him - he’s your dad, and if he loves you, he is still going to NOT want you to get sick or worse. Wear your mask, even at home… research shows there is a big spread amongst families whose members eat together and do things together, live watch tv, if they do it without masks. It seems weird to do it, but my family is doing it. Masks cannot control every little risk about this pandemic, but it slows transmission rates, even at home, among family members, as does the hand washing for more than 20 seconds… and keeping up with other hygiene, and laundry cycling on hot water and hot air for drying, and disinfecting high-touch surfaces like door knobs, faucet and drawer pulls and handles, light switches, electronic devices, and so on and so forth. See what you can do to contribute, and find sources of real support where you can let your hair down and get things off your chest… don’t try to resolve a bunch of family stuff right now. We’re all on docks that are shifting in the water and some of our docks’ posts are coming loose from their mooring. Give things time… I think Fall 2021 we will all be much better off and wiser. Now, however, is NOT the time to let up. Keep up all your efforts. In your heart of hearts, try to just take time to remind yourself of all that you value about your dad and other family members, and how much you have to look forward to, to live for, and to do in life, so that you can keep your motivation HIGH (and your example SUPERIOR) til this thing is over.

Question: How do you keep yourself safe if you live with people who aren’t adhering to safety guidelines during the COVID-19 pandemic?
Answer: Trust your OWN counsel on this. For my son and me when he was working at WAL-Mart, we even began to wear masks at home if we were out in the small family room hanging out - as studies were showing this was where and when transmission between family members and/or roommates took place frequently. People might say “Oh, that’s ridiculous! We shouldn’t ‘HAVE TO’ do THAT!” Well, maybe not, but better masked up than dead. No one but you can gauge what is appropriate for you, in terms of precautions and if others can’t handle the VERY TEMPORARY imposition on their own convenience and help you protect your health, go to your room and close the door; use a copper mask for a couple hours before nodding off to sleep (copper kills all corona viruses and even HIV) and celebrate everyday you get up without being sick! The point is to SURVIVE this thing and live to pass on YOUR wisdom on how you did it to the next generation… Do what it takes; STAND YOUR GROUND. It is okay to take precautions. It is okay to be different and it is important to live to tell others later how to get through stuff like this. You’re well on your way to being a winner on this issue. Keep up the good work. Do your part and trust God to help for the parts of it that you cannot control.

Question: Would you be concerned if you see your atheist friend beginning to pray during the coronavirus outbreak?

Then I would evaluate what seems like my most helpful response could be. Their sudden pleas to God during this viral outbreak would have no influence whatsoever on my sense of security or fear about the outbreak. I take my stuff to God, because my experience is that He’s the one with the shoulders that can handle it. I would just want my friend to be okay, on whatever terms they decide to be okay. Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is one piece of simple advice that actually changed your life?
Answer: There is an unhappy record of suicide in three generations on my dad’s family’s side… now, keep in mind, nothing is an absolute, and in each of these cases, there was not just a parent from my father’s line, but also a parent from another family line, but the stats are not good: 1) My father’s cousin committed suicide in her 70’s - started a fire in the townhouse when no one else (thankfully) was there. 2) My father’s brother’s eldest son committed suicide in his late 20’s. 3) My father’s brother’s other son had a son, who at age 17, a day or two off Prozac for depression, committed suicide. In none of these cases was alcohol a habit. Therefore, one of the best pieces of advice I ever got related to why no one would want to become a suicide if they knew some important facts up front. The advice giver, an exegetical bible study teacher/pastor, explained suicide is the biggest joke, in hell: “The” Devil laughs because he knows suicide cuts short the rewards we WILL get on Earth, no matter how long we live or how much we suffer, as well as the rewards we will get in Heaven.” I reaped from this man’s input two profound benefits: First, I recognized suicide as a thing, a force, an event, that was “beyond” me… that I possibly could not control its rising up or its eventuality. This gave me humility in the face of it as a threat to my life and to any possibly good outcome in my life. Humility in turn, if desire to confound a thing rather than to be confounded by it is present, allows for one to study to become more prepared to deal with possible risk. Second, it helped me gain objectivity… that is, it helped me see the thing, suicide, as something that in a sense, that plays a role, possibly, in SOMEONE ELSE’S PLANS. That piece of news helped because when it comes to THAT player, “the devil,” I was not motivated to agree with his plans. In fact, I should like to rob him of anything and everything that he thinks he has coming to him. Therefore, whenever I have had to deal with my own tendency toward depression, which got acutely bad after my son was born, for literally about four to five years, and then later on for a couple years as I neared the age of 60, I was conscious of the risks involved in letting myself get too low. It prompted me to be both conscious about my state of mind, AND about attempting to activate some “possibility” thinking about addressing those low feelings BEFORE they ripened into something worse. I appreciate being asked to contribute to this library of answers on this question about advice and truly hope it benefits someone who might also be facing a challenge in this area of life.

Question: When a vaccine is available for Covid-19, will you be comfortable enough to get it? What would your reason be for not wanting it?
Answer: The last time I was seriously ill with a contagious disease was in Fall 1993; it was some sort of flu, and the coughing was horrendous. I sat on the floor in my bedroom, trying to decide between calling the ambulance or chancing dying, the coughing was so bad, it seemed my lungs were closing right up. I was praying like crazy, and it was either this stops or I have to call an ambulance. OMGosh I was fearful, for sure. And all of a sudden, it stopped. I wasn’t all the way well, but that coughing stopped. Today, 26 and a half years later, I sit being para-symptomatic… where I “think” I may have “caught” “it;” where my throat or lungs “just don’t feel right,” or maybe I’m slightly hot, or whatever! I have never relied on the flu vaccine to not get the flu; but I have always been careful to keep my distance from other shoppers at grocery stores, and other places where folks congregate during flu season. So, while I may have skipped the flu vaccine from time to time, if the scientists come up with a vaccine for this bug, tell me when and where and I’ll be there. The risks of the downside of this bug are just to severe, uncontrolled as of yet by any therapeutic process in a reliable manner, so to me it will be quite well worth it. Meanwhile, I’m masking up and staying home and bugging my essential worker roommate to take off his shoes and clothes at the door to have them sanitized while he jumps in the shower. It isn’t over yet, and I do not want to become a proverb of being unwilling to suffer a little to avoid all this plague’s disastrous potential. It is nice, however, to think of a time when we will no longer have anything to fear about SARS2. Thinking ahead to a vaccine helped me do that tonight, so thank you, Perry, for including me in your A2A.

Question: My friend hasn't been answering his phone for 2 months saying he's going off the grid. I know I'm not the problem but I am really worried about his mental state. What should I do?
Answer: Be normal. Be normal person during an abnormal time. Many people are nervous, depressed, anxious, uncomfortable, at time feel like they’re coming apart at the seams. Be the normal friend. Don’t worry about him. Establish a routine of emailing, or drop him a funny meme to his home address. Emphasize when you do talk to him that while things are still very weird, they will not stay this way forever. If he’s up for a joke, tease him that they’ll probably get worse… but only if he’s up for a laugh. You still care about your friend; that is normal… And then, try and see, if he does return the favor of contacting you too, get him to talk about something he is interested in. Your job is just to be a friend.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Have you ever known someone that was healed by faith?
Answer: Is it wrong to answer a question with a question? If not, here is the beginning of my questions for you: Did Jesus walk “by faith” across the Sea of Galilee? Or something else? If it was something else, was it something, “material?” Like an invisible cloak? If it was an invisible cloak, can we put that on? Can we “walk on water” while standing on such a thing? Are carbon nanotubes willing to be at our command if we have faith? Would it be the same thing or things that helped the Monks of Skellig build a steep path of stones up the side of Skellig Michael, a crag in the British Isles, 1300 years ago? Do I stay well because I “believe” I am, or will be well? Or because I acknowledge God is in me and He doesn’t get sick, period? So, do I know someone who was healed “by faith?” Does that mean “faith healing…” like someone laid hands on them and they got well? I can tell you this. I have met two people who “had” multiple sclerosis and in the case of one, then in her 70’s when I met her, she had been free from MS symptoms ever since she had, what she experienced as a healing from God… no big event, just as a “result” of her faith in God and she believed God healed her, more than 20 years prior. A second man, Elery Mayo, a Vietnam Marine Veteran, (see some clips here if you can: https://vimeo.com/user5873730 was “saved” in Christ, in 1973, but in one year, he was in and out of a wheel chair, paralyzed, blind, with doctors trying to figure out what “it” was, and eventually finding out it was MS. Now Elery believed the Lord, he had faith, and he KNEW the words in the Good Book were true, that whosoever believed on Jesus and followed him would indeed do the same works, AND BETTER, Jesus said, but it can take some time… it is a learning process. He explained that this learning process as it applied to his body and disease, took “seven years to learn to walk in the healing that Jesus died for us to have access to…” So, as Elery put it, “Now, if they x-rayed my grey matter, they might still find those plaques… they were still there the last time I got those pictures… “ but the last time was more than a decade ago… “but fact is, the only time I get symptoms is if someone comes up who is trying to get healed from MS.” My own personal introduction to what I might call the physics of faith (though I am not talking just in terms of what might be some of the thinking in “Christian Science”) was through Elery… he taught the SUPRA-natural world behind this one… and gradually I have gotten more and more into the Spirit. God is big on not just believing in him (the “devils believe and tremble…” but we know where they live), but in obeying him. The closer we STAY to him, the more we can walk in a way where illness is not common. For me this is how it works: We must remember our position in God. He is our FATHER, it’s not just a metaphor; it’s REAL. IF WE ARE HIS SONS, then we can do what he does, PERIOD. But it does take practice; harnessing control over our emotions and thought life is the elusive key, but bible reading, fellowship with other believers in Christ, and related activities, like just doing what’s good for you and others, helps. Thanks for the A2A, Mike S.

Question: Why can young Americans get very sick from Covid-19?
Answer: Young Americans can get very sick from CoVid-19 because of underlying conditions, just as some older people do. And, age and underlying medical or health conditions like heart disease and diabetes are not the only things that this virus can take advantage of. For some reason, some people who catch CoVid-19 will develop an exacerbated response to the threat to their health and overproduce cells and accelerate processes related to inflammation, making it harder for the body to actually fight the virus. Lungs, even young ones that are not compromised before the virus, can be tread upon by the pace at which this virus replicates and quickly require help to keep bringing fresh oxygen in and pushing carbon dioxide out. Unfortunately for some young people who have had CoVid-19, their lungs and other organs were overcome and they expired before science or medical efforts have become effective enough to help them win the battle. This is ANOTHER reason why we should wear our masks when we go outside to places where we may run into others. It REALLY isn’t a terrible inconvenience. It IS an annoyance, but what’s that compared to saving the life of someone’s grandfather? Mother?? Sister? Yourself?

Question: Why are people so convinced that going to church in person is essential?
Answer: I’m afraid that I would have to conclude that many people who are convinced that going to church and assembling with others, many others, is “essential,” right now in particular, are hooked into an ego-based conviction, and not the conviction of the Holy Spirit (which is what SHOULD govern their decision-making), and that this ego-hook, if you will, is about proving their faith to the world. Now, many of these church-goers will also state that they are just trying to do what the Word of God says (Hebrews 10:25 King Jim version: “Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.”); In their minds, they are being obedient to a “Higher Authority,” and this too is a wind that serves to fluff their feathers in an effort to prove to themselves at least that they are diligent, sincere, real, Christian men and women. But, interestingly enough, when you feel your status in something is determinant upon what other people see and think about you, you have already lost the battle. Faith is OFTEN NOT what it looks like to others. In the most faithful act in history, except perhaps for agreeing to be born, Christ allowing himself to be put up on that Cross at Calvary, to MANY others, it looked like the work of a fool. After all, if you ARE GOD, why wouldn’t your first act on that cross be jumping down and slaying all the Roman guard around you and then pounding heat against the Sanhedrin that illegally arrested him and saw him punished for no sin whatsoever? But that was not the point. The point ISN’T POWER; if it was, then the world’s constant search, at great expense of human life and national treasuries, would have yielded the world’s best weapon, the way to be permanently secure from attack, and so forth. But that isn’t how history reveals the end of those futile missions, is it? If it isn’t, then what is the point of it all? The POINT is LOVE of course, but other “religions” propose kindness and other things akin to LOVE, AND THE POINT is to LIVE THE KINGDOM LIFE: REIGN FROM ABOVE. WALK ON THAT WATER. REACH OUT YOUR HAND AND HEAL THE SICK. Those things are not accomplished with an earthy mindset, they are accomplished when someone is beyond convinced of the temporal realities being subject to something far greater and that they too are called to subject the temporal world to themselves. These people do not allow themselves to be bound by compunction - by the “order” that comes up inside them to prove something, like that they love God and they will serve God, and they will be at church come hell or high water. Unfortunately, that is still legalism, and has no ability to give lift-off to the truth of the Word of God that came to set us free from entanglement with a hollow virtue that has a hollow ring of truth, but no power within. Diligence is NOT a substitute for relationship with God. Only God can be God in your life, not the bible, not a pastor, not your traditions, not rules, never compunction. Dying to self (including the need to STOP taking refuge or any self-satisfaction from these things) is not fun AND it takes a LOT of work to connect with all three persons of the trinity - with God - and it takes a LOT of work to clear out our stuff, to take every thought captive to Christ, and NO ONE else but YOU can do this work. NO ONE. Therefore, if you’re going to church to prove God’s will today, on Pentecost, and if you’re thinking you’re happily One With Your President, and it all feels good and right, know that there will yet be another football thrown into your end of the field, and you will have to get up again, grab that pigskin, and find a way to get it to the other end of the field. As for me and mine, we will serve the Lord; we will grind out the grist that is unacceptable to him; and we will not harbor illusions that “trying hard,” is what pleases God. He has made it clear, time and time again, what pleases God is FAITH.

Question: What is the most effective way of asking for financial help?
Answer: Determining what is the best way to ask for financial help can be complicated, depending on the asker’s status, ability to pay back if any, purposes of the help, habits of asking for help in the past, ability of the giver/lender, likelihood and frequency of how often the giver/lender one is approaching has to deal with people or organizations coming to them for help. The most successful scenarios depend on the asker’s character and record of production within the community they are going to for help. If, for instance, you are a fantastic volunteer at your church, and have been tithing and an active member for several years, IF the church doesn’t have a policy against it, this person may find their need quickly met. I recall my father, a 13-year old when the Depression hit the USA in 1932, telling about the “only” time he ever borrowed money from someone other going to a bank for establishing a mortgage on a piece of real estate. It was 1945; he had been back from the war for two years, had two children as well as two step children off and on, and had been working for Alexander Film Company as a pilot and then in sales. He had earned a Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration from the Colorado College before he signed up for the Air Corps, so he knew well the value of a dollar SAVED, and that renting was a losing proposition. A small house on Harrison Street came up for sale just a few blocks from the film company’s buildings on North Nevada Avenue, and it had a good price. He approached a man he worked with who was familiar with his work ethic and abilities, and indeed secured a personal loan of $3,000 to put down on what would become his home. By then immediately dividing the place in to an upstairs-downstairs duplex, and securing a solid couple to rent from him, he was able to pay that man back in short order, securing another step in establishing a good reputation which continued to build and be stable over a lifetime of living. If, Tim, you asked this due to the number of needs that may be arising out of COVID-19 based unemployment or paychecks missing in action, I think the best approach is to have a plan of how the need is not going to be reoccurring, because one thing many helpers do not want to do is “throw money down the drain.” Therefore, having a plan of how one will not need this money in the future, and explaining your creative ways and past ways of meeting such difficulties and overcoming them should help. IF someone anticipates needing such help, I would go NOW and ask, because if the COVID-19 situation lasts for a long time, or worsens, people are going to hold back on giving due to their own concerns as trouble comes lapping at their doors, and they will have already given as much as they can, AND their donations will be dropping severely in most cases during this time period. The other key thing about getting help, to me, is asking God first whether and how to meet a problem or need. If, after seeking such counsel, one feels free to ask for help, then do it with the resolve that you are going to get it, no matter what person #1, or person #2, or organization #3, say to you. Don’t let other people’s misgivings about you or helping others get in the way. That’s their issue, not yours. If you need help, go get it. There are plenty of people who have more than enough, and there are people who regardless of how much they have, they will help.

Question: How will researchers connect these Covid-19 clues: 1.patients with home care less mortality than hospitalized; 2.virus doesn't enter ambiotic fluid; 3.virus is not transmitted by breast milk, or 4.some animals are more vulnerable to infection?
Answer: Please allow me to only throw my hat in this ring in order to put forward a basic guess which many people surely already have surmised as well, and that is regarding clue 1. : “patients with home care less mortality than hospitalized.” The link to a FINANCIAL TIMES article that evinces a stark contrast between the death rates from COVID-19 in Lombardy and Veneto, Italy; is great, but only remotely touches on the “clue,” listed above as one of four that the Quora writer would like to see how the scientific world will connect the dots. The fact is, in many scientific studies, factors which at first seem as though they must fit together actually do not. And in fact they are not infrequently unrelated altogether; kind of like a man not talking to his wife after work one day. She thinks it’s something she said; he keeps saying, “Yes, dear,” but to his consternation, his commitment to being congenial, agreeable only works to worsen his account of goodwill from his wife, because as the evening progresses, the glass of wine he served her is apparently going to be totally wasted, which is a pity because now that he has figured out the answer to the problem from work that came home with him in his head, she looks pretty much like she’s only going to offer him a cold shoulder the rest of the night. Just under 100 miles apart, the people of Veneto and Lombardy are themselves having some trouble related to a glass of wine - for they are worlds apart thus far with respect to how many people are celebrating over a cup of fine Italian vino or drowning their valid sorrows with it. According to the Financial Times article, Lombardy has lost 8,576 of its good citizens, (which in total number more than 10 million) while Veneto, a city of half the population of Lombardy) have lost only 607 of their loved ones out of 10,824 diagnosed cases. Lombardy’s death rate of 17.6 per cent, in other words, is more than triple that of Veneto’s, at 5.6 percent. But as the FT article elucidates, the key to understanding and therefore avoiding the duplication of Lombardy’s comparative disadvantage isn’t in the detection of some elusive characteristic of the biological treasures within the people of Veneto; no, the answer clearly lies in the cities’ differing attitudes and resulting rates of hospital admissions of those suffering from COVID-19. Again, from Financial Times : “The number of diagnosed patients who were taken in hospitals for clinical treatment at the start of the outbreak was about 65 per cent in Lombardy, Prof Palù said. This compares with 20 per cent in Veneto, where the majority were told to stay at home unless urgent care was required. “There were different instructions given to the sick by the different regional health authorities,” he said. “Yes, there has been more testing in Veneto but people were kept at home and not taken into hospitals. The more patients you admit to the hospital, the more cases you get. You create the outbreak as at the start nobody was taking care of sampling the doctors or nurses, [so] you were taking home the infection. “His observation comes as more than 60 Italian doctors and health workers have died, the majority of these in Lombardy. A group of doctors from the Papa Giovanni XXIII hospital in Bergamo warned last month that hospitals had become the main source of transmission of Covid-19 infections, and urged more patients to be treated at home.”) SO, don’t concentrate the opportunities for infection, or shall we say, infestation. Prevalence of the virus, the viral load, the number of viral particles in the air, on the surfaces, this seems to be the issue most germane to Lombardy’s death rate? And, isn’t the “sub-issue” the way that health professionals are acting as “spreading agents” for the disease as their work environments are massively occupied with COVID-19 positive human beings? If previously assumed models of the distance viral-carrying droplets can spew through your living room or your office have underestimated the power of your sneezing reflexes, (as MIT seemed to have recently shown: [A high speed camera at MIT is showing that a sneeze can travel up to 8m, four times the distance of theoretical models used in the Covid-19 outbreak [Researchers at MIT in the US have used a high speed imaging camera to show that a sneeze carrying the Covid-19 virus can travel up to 8m. This is four times the distance previously predicted and has significant implications for social distances and the design of equipment.] …then aren’t we TOTALLY in the Wild Wild West of Guess Work Ranch when it comes to measuring the viral contamination of PPE and transference from one surface to one human hand, to one human knee, to one bed rail, to a hospital bed and so forth???? I think we are. And of course, the Quora question poser knows that this slice of life is only a teeny percentage of all that might be up for consideration under Clue 1: Home care better outcomes than hospital care for COVID-19′ers. Is it being able to SEE and TOUCH your loved ones when you feel you might DIE that is making the difference? Are we contrasting nursing homes to hospitals? Are we contrasting private nurses and doctors paid to come in to a home who aren’t stressed out with making decisions over who shall live and die every day? And what about that social support? Is that what made the difference with the 17 church goers in Singapore who ALL got better from COVID even after a few got really, really, bad? How They Beat Coronavirus! As to Clues 2 (virus doesn’t enter amniotic fluid) and 3 (virus is not transmitted in breast milk), I believe these will be found to be attributable to physical features of the virus as well as the biochemical mechanisms in the placenta and the fetus. Clue 4, “Some animals are more vulnerable to infection,” since this will first be understood on a macro level, as in which SPECIES are more vulnerable to infection, and is that the same thing as getting sick, as opposed to trying to draw up parallels between individual animals of identical species. Comments, opinions, additions, criticisms, all are welcome on this one. I find the question inordinately tempting to direct my entire intellectual life for a few days. I love puzzles!

Question: Do you call an Anglican priest Father?
Answer: Yeah, if you are sucked into that sort of thing. I personally believe Jesus’ injunction AGAINST calling people Father or Rabbi/Teacher was serious… and it was meant to prevent the misuse of the understanding of personal psychology to bind people into emotional dependence upon people, not God. This thing, calling people “Father” or Priest or Rabbi… Jesus Himself, King of Kings, said, “Do not call me that…. I am your friend…. Do not call ANYONE that…” He was serious about it. It screws us up BIG time, because one of the BIGGEST “temptations” of adulthood is either never leaving childhood behind, or regressing back into dependency. Jesus knew what he was talking about. So, how about obeying Jesus’ words instead of human convention, and tell the priest you wish to follow what the Lord said. You might even go farther and say that you acknowledge him (the priest) as your EQUAL, no more, no less, and that you would like to be friends. That’s what JESUS himself wanted to be to his disciples; how could anyone else expect or train others to walk in some other calling than that?

Name: Sara Stone
Question: Why do so many pastors and churches have a disconnect with science? Why are so many not following the stay at home orders and opening the church up during this Coronavirus/Covid-19 pandemic?
Answer: It’s a little hard to understand it, isn’t it? It is like to some of those people they feel THEIR OWN PERSONAL FAITH is being tested by God (or that their own “flock” will find them LACKING). I am glad that in Colorado Springs the vast majority of churches are being closed; this isn’t an issue about healing not being available at church or through people who have faith in Christ; this is about not tempting faith AND submitting to governmental authority. The very first thing this defiance does is lose face for the church. The pastors that do this aren’t showing how good God or they are; they are showing that they think it’s okay to do whatever you want despite what your government says. This is quite unfortunate, and I am afraid it WILL and has ALREADY cost people lives. The way I have observed that most churches work is that they follow a certain set of guidelines and doctrinal positions in suit with what their individual denominational leaders and councils advise; so IF their “leaders” that are beyond their local pulpit say, “Hey the “dark state” government, or whatever, is trying to take control of all of us… then they fall in line and do what is suggested, which, perhaps is involved with those churches who have chosen NOT to shutter their doors. You think of how the early Christians “worshiped,” IN PEOPLE’S homes; there were no large places to meet, except occasionally, and then often in a rich person’s home. We have become awfully conditioned to think everything today has to be just like it was yesterday, and that, I think, is one very GOOD thing this COVID-19 will do… it just might shake things up enough to unhook people from their expectations and get them down to brass tacks about their lives. You’ve contended that this trend of keeping churches open is actually about a rift between men and women of science and men and women of, apparently in your mind, faith-and-therefore-no-science, but I don’t think that is the case with all. I say that because of an article Quora writer Judy Dodd brought my attention to about 44 rabbis dying since COVID-19 began, most of them in the USA. Rabbis are NOT anti-science. But convictions about their faith and meeting together are very strong. It caused me to reconsider that all such decisions to stay open were born of anti-scientism and instead entertain the thought that this may just be about deep convictions. The question about the separation of church and science, is really, an entirely different question than it in the context of decisions during COVID-19. And it is WAY too big of a question to add on thoughts about it right here. Ask the question separately and I will give it a go, Tony. Thanks for including me in your A2A.

Question: Are people getting more aggressive because of the quarantine?
Answer: Subconscious material, conflicts, are bubbling up to the surface, with less and less to distract us. A distraction only lasts a little while… Then one must have a new distraction, at least for a little while; after nearly 120 days of rotating through such “distractions,” it is impossible for most of us to keep that subconscious stuff buried, and with no normal outlets to let off steam and then process, some of us might be getting a little bit more than on edge. And, for those individuals or groups of individuals, or community of individuals who practice repression as a chief way of coping with unpleasant realities, they (or we) may be most apt to “have” more anger than others. Sound familiar? It is DEFINITELY what I am dealing with. And it’s frustrating. Thanks for the A2A. Stay safe, keep wearing those masks!
